scenes.say: How do you make sure your services always speak the same language and avoid nasty integration bugs?

scenes.label: Contract
scenes.sub: An agreement on how services interact
scenes.say: A contract is just an agreement on how two services talk to each other. It defines what requests and responses look like.
First, the consumer writes a contract describing what it expects. The provider then tests its real API against that contract. Tools like Pact automate this for you.

scenes.title: Pact test run
scenes.say: Here's a Pact test in action. It checks that GET user returns the right fields, and the provider confirms the contract matches its implementation.

scenes.question: Does contract testing replace integration tests?
scenes.right: No. Contract tests check interfaces; integration tests check real interactions.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: contract tests don't replace integration tests. Contracts check the interface, but integration tests check real-world interactions.
